source.title: Soft and elastic hydrogel-based microelectronics for localized low-voltage neuromodulation

material: PEDOT:PSS electrically conductive hydrogel (ECH) from ionic-liquid ion gel after water exchange

formulation.evidence: Approximately 50wt% of ionic liquid versus PEDOT:PSS was added to PEDOT:PSS aqueous solution (0.172 g in 15ml of PH1000 solution)

processing.evidence: the filtered PEDOT:PSS–ionic liquid solution was spun coated on SiO2, PFPE or PDMS substrate at a speed of 2,000 r.p.m. for 1min, followed by annealing at 130 °C for 30min
the film was soaked in a copious amount of deionized water (Millipore water purification system) for over 24h

youngs_modulus.evidence: The Young’s modulus values of the ECH were estimated to be 32±5.1 kPa when measured via compression tests

conductivity.evidence: Our ECH has an electrical conductivity of 47.4±1.2 S cm−1

water_content.evidence: The water content in the hydrogel was estimated to be ~82wt% within 1min of soaking in water

description.value: only slight decrease in UV–visible absorption at 800 nm
description.evidence: after 48h of soaking in water, the ECH film showed only a slight decrease in UV–visible absorption intensity

duration_days.evidence: after 48h of soaking in water, the ECH film showed only a slight decrease in UV–visible absorption intensity

stability.conditions: thin film (1.4 µm) soaked in water

notes: Hydrated in water. CSC 164 mC cm−2. 200 nm films sustained 20% strain; <20% impedance increase at 1 kHz under 10% strain. PEDOT/PSS ratio 0.4 to 0.78 after washing.
